name: Alampur — the Navabrahma Temples and Jogulamba
theme: Nine early Chalukya temples of Shiva and the Shakti Peetha of Jogulamba on the Tungabhadra near its meeting with the Krishna
region: Telangana (Jogulamba Gadwal district, on the Tungabhadra)
description: At Alampur, on the bank of the Tungabhadra a little above its meeting with the Krishna, stands a group of nine Shiva temples built by the Badami Chalukyas in the 7th and 8th centuries: the Navabrahma temples, named Bala, Taraka, Swarga, Padma, Garuda, Kumara, Arka, Vira and Vishwa Brahma. With their curvilinear northern-style towers they show the Chalukya builders working in the same experimental spirit as at Aihole and Pattadakal, and their sculpture is among the finest of the age. Beside them stands the temple of Jogulamba, one of the eighteen Maha Shakti Peethas, so that Alampur is at once a living pilgrimage and a monument of early Indian temple architecture, cared for by the Archaeological Survey of India.
